title: Per-shard locking in a sharded search index
name: Sharded index rebalancer

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code acquires shard locks? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: moveDocument nests withShard(fromShard) then withShard(toShard), so it acquires locks in argument order rather than the sorted order withShards uses. A rebalancing plan run with 8 concurrent workers can easily contain a move A->B and a move B->A at the same time: one holds A waiting for B, the other holds B waiting for A, and both await forever. mergeShards running alongside (sorted order) can also be caught in the cycle. Since AsyncMutex has no timeout, the workers hang silently. Using `this.locks.withShards([fromShard, toShard], ...)` fixes it.

choiceQuestions.prompt: In AsyncMutex.acquire, what happens when three callers call acquire() on an unlocked mutex in the same tick?
choices: All three get the lock at once because tail is already resolved
They get it one at a time in call order; each waits on the previous caller's release
The order is unspecified because promises resolve in random order
The second and third calls throw because the lock is held
choiceQuestions.explanation: Each call captures prev = this.tail synchronously and replaces tail with prev.then(() => next), so callers form a FIFO chain: caller 2 awaits caller 1's release promise, caller 3 awaits caller 2's. Only the first awaits an already-resolved promise; promise resolution order is deterministic, and nothing throws.

choiceQuestions.prompt: mergeShards is called with sourceShards = ["shard-002", "shard-002"] and target "shard-002". What happens?
choices: It deadlocks because shard-002 is locked twice
It throws because a shard cannot be merged into itself
It acquires shard-002 once and returns 0 without touching storage
It deletes every document in shard-002
choiceQuestions.explanation: withShards dedupes via new Set before acquiring, so the non-reentrant mutex is taken only once. Inside, every src equals target and is skipped by `continue`, so moved stays 0. There is no explicit check that throws, and no remove is reached.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Two upsert calls for the same doc arrive concurrently with updatedAt 200 and 100, and the 100 call happens to acquire the shard lock first. What ends up stored?
choices: Whichever finished its storage.write last, nondeterministically
Neither; the second call is rejected because the lock is held
choiceQuestions.explanation: upsert performs load-compare-write inside withShard, so the calls are serialized. The 100 version is written first; then the 200 call loads it, sees existing.updatedAt (100) is not greater than 200, and writes. Had the order been reversed, the 100 call would see a newer version and return without writing. Lock contention queues callers rather than rejecting them.
